questions.prompt: Derive the equation of motion for $C^R_{AB}(t)=-i\theta(t)\langle[A(t),B]\rangle$ and write it in frequency space.
questions.solution:
Differentiating $\theta(t)$ gives $\delta(t)\langle[A,B]\rangle$, and $i\partial_tA(t)=[A,H](t)$ (since $\partial_tA=i[H,A]$). The result is
$$(\omega+i\eta)\,C^R_{AB}(\omega)=\langle[A,B]\rangle+C^R_{[A,H],B}(\omega).$$
For fermions the commutator in the first term is an anticommutator.

questions.prompt: In the wide-band limit a single level coupled to a continuum has spectral function
questions.solution: Eq. (9.22) with the constant coupling of Eq. (9.40) gives $\Sigma^R\approx -i\Gamma/2$ plus a real shift (Eq. 9.41), so $A=\Gamma/[(\omega-\tilde\xi_0)^2+\Gamma^2/4]$, a Lorentzian of full width $\Gamma$ (Eq. 9.42). A delta peak would need zero coupling, and a Gaussian is not produced by a constant self-energy.

questions.prompt: Why does the EOM for the Anderson model not close, and what does the mean-field approximation do?
questions.solution: Commuting $d_\sigma$ with the interaction $Un_{d\uparrow}n_{d\downarrow}$ produces $n_{d\bar\sigma}d_\sigma$, a two-particle Green's function $D^R$ (Eqs. 9.30-9.34). Its own equation of motion generates yet another function, so the set does not close. Mean field replaces $n_{d\bar\sigma}$ by $\langle n_{d\bar\sigma}\rangle$, which gives a level shifted to $\varepsilon_d+U\langle n_{\bar\sigma}\rangle$ (Eqs. 9.35-9.38).

questions.prompt: The RPA density response of the electron gas is
questions.solution: Eq. (9.57) follows from the equation of motion for $\chi^R(kq,\omega)$ truncated in the random phase approximation (Eqs. 9.54-9.56), giving $\chi_0/(1-V\chi_0)$. The option $\chi_0(1-V\chi_0)$ has the wrong structure (no pole from the interaction), and the others do not reduce to $\chi_0$ for $V\to0$.

questions.prompt: Ex. 9.1. Two orbitals have $H=E_1c^\dagger_1c_1+E_2c^\dagger_2c_2+t\,c^\dagger_1c_2+t^*c^\dagger_2c_1$. Use the EOM to find $G^R_{11}(\omega)$ and $G^R_{21}(\omega)$, and interpret the poles.
questions.solution:
Book Exercise 9.1. In the basis $(1,2)$ the EOM (Eq. 9.10a) is a $2\times2$ matrix equation. Inverting gives
$$G^R_{11}(\omega)=\frac{\omega-E_2}{(\omega-E_1)(\omega-E_2)-|t|^2},\qquad G^R_{21}(\omega)=\frac{t^*}{(\omega-E_1)(\omega-E_2)-|t|^2}.$$
The poles are at $E_\pm=\frac{E_1+E_2}{2}\pm\sqrt{\left(\frac{E_1-E_2}{2}\right)^2+|t|^2}$, the bonding and antibonding levels. The residues give the weight of orbital 1 in each eigenstate.

questions.prompt: Ex. 9.2. Derive the EOM relations of Eqs. (9.30)-(9.31) by differentiating the Green's functions of Eq. (9.28). Show the dot and lead equations.
questions.solution:
Book Exercise 9.2. With the book's hybridization $t_kc^\dagger_{d\sigma}c_{k\sigma}+t_k^*c^\dagger_{k\sigma}c_{d\sigma}$ (Eq. 9.25), compute $[d_\sigma,H]$ and $[c_{k\sigma},H]$. The commutators give
$$(\omega+i\eta-\varepsilon_d+\mu)\,G^R(d\sigma,\omega)-\sum_kt_k\,G^R(k\sigma,d\sigma,\omega)=1+U\,D^R(d\sigma,\omega),\qquad (\omega+i\eta-\varepsilon_k+\mu)\,G^R(k\sigma,d\sigma,\omega)=t_k^*\,G^R(d\sigma,\omega),$$
with $D^R=\langle\langle n_{d\bar\sigma}d_\sigma;d^\dagger_\sigma\rangle\rangle$. The first equation uses $[d_\sigma,Un_{d\uparrow}n_{d\downarrow}]=Un_{d\bar\sigma}d_\sigma$.

questions.prompt: Ex. 9.3. An STM tip sits over an adatom described by the Anderson model. The tip-to-atom tunneling is described by Eq. (8.65). Show that $dI/dV$ measures the adatom spectral function, and state its mean-field form.
questions.solution: Book Exercise 9.3. The tunneling current of Eq. (8.74) with a flat tip density of states gives $dI/dV\propto A_d(-eV)$ (Eq. 8.77, for the book's $V=V_1-V_2$). In mean field (Sec. 9.3.2) the adatom spectral function is, for each spin, a Lorentzian of full width $\Gamma$ centered at $\omega=\tilde\varepsilon-\mu+U\langle n_{\bar\sigma}\rangle$ (Eq. 9.42), so $dI/dV$ shows one peak per spin. Without magnetization the two peaks coincide.

questions.prompt: From the self-consistency condition of Eq. (9.45) in the symmetric case $x=1/2$, find the condition for a magnetic solution with $\langle n_\uparrow\rangle\neq\langle n_\downarrow\rangle$.
questions.solution:
Put $\langle n_{\uparrow,\downarrow}\rangle=\tfrac12\pm\delta$. Then $\cot(\pi\langle n_\uparrow\rangle)=-\tan(\pi\delta)$ and the right side is $(\langle n_\downarrow\rangle-\tfrac12)y=-y\delta$, so
$$\tan(\pi\delta)=y\,\delta.$$
The ratio $\tan(\pi\delta)/\delta$ rises monotonically from $\pi$ at $\delta\to0$ to infinity at $\delta\to\tfrac12$. A non-zero root therefore exists exactly when $y>\pi$, that is $U>\pi\Gamma/2$.
